description: Band-pass filters the spectrum by zeroing/attenuating channels outside the frq1-frq2 band, with Q setting the width of the filter skirts in Hz. Pinned to mode 7 (band pass) of the 12-mode family: 1/3 high/low pass, 2/4/8/10 normalised variants, 5/6/11/12 add a gain positional, 9 notch - all six surveyed modes verified running with the expected spectral direction (centroids: HP 1674 Hz, LP 504, BP 1003, notch 697 on a 700 Hz-centroid probe). Reversed band edges are silently swapped (2000/500 byte-identical to 500/2000). frq1, frq2 and Q all breakpoint-capable (each ramp differs from both scalar-endpoint renders; banner-confirmed). Static duration; deterministic. Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: Filtering INSIDE the analysis domain, which behaves differently from a time-domain EQ: channels are zeroed outright, so deep settings produce the hollow, resynthesised 'spectral filter' sound rather than an analog slope. Time-varying edges are the real attraction - breakpoint frq1/frq2 into converging or sweeping trajectories for formant-like motion and telephone-band chokes that a static EQ cannot articulate per-window. Q is the skirt width in Hz: small Q = hard spectral cliff (maximum hollowness), large Q = gentler shading. For the notch complement use mode 9 via execute(); for level-compensated variants the normalised modes (8/10) rescale output energy. On already-analysed chains it saves a resynthesis round-trip versus dropping to the time domain for EQ.

frq1.description: Lower band edge. CDP-enforced 10 to nyquist ('0' refused verbatim: 'Parameter[1] Value (0.000000) out of range (10.000000 to 22050.000000)'). If frq1 > frq2 the pair is silently swapped (byte-identical output, verified). Breakpoint verified (300-to-900 ramp differs from both endpoints).

frq2.description: Upper band edge, same enforced range (Parameter[2] refusal verbatim at 30000). Breakpoint verified (1500-to-4000 ramp differs from both endpoints).

q.description: Width of the filter skirts in Hz (banner: 'Range: >0'; CDP actually enforces 1 to 22050 - '0' and '100000' refused verbatim quoting '(1.000000 to 22050.000000)'). Small = cliff edge, large = soft shading. Breakpoint verified (20-to-300 ramp differs from both endpoints).

examples.expected_use: Telephone-band spectral choke with moderate skirts.
The pass band narrows from wide-open to a 800-1200 Hz slot across the file - formant-like focusing.

known_issues: Reversed band edges are accepted and silently swapped (byte-identical to the ordered pair) - no warning is printed.
Q's banner claims only '> 0'; the binary enforces 1 to 22050 Hz (refusals verbatim).
Modes 1-6 and 8-12 (high/low pass, normalised, gain and notch variants) verified running - reachable via execute(['hilite', 'filter', '<mode>', ...]); the gain modes append a 4th positional.
